page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes or footnotes.

main_text.p: Opponct fe adverfus quicquid dicitur Deus aut numen, σέβασμα[?], id quod colitur, hoc eft, adverfus quascunq; poteftates & majeftates, tam terreftres, quàm cæleftes. Ut enim diabolus adverfarius eft Deo, ideoque Satan appellatur: fic Antichriftus adverfarius eft Deo & Chrifto, atque hinc Antichrifti nomen obtinuit. Hæc oppofitio quam prædixit Apoftolus, ita propria eft Antichrifto, ut quicunque demum is fit, qui opponit fe adverfus quicquid dicitur Deus aut numen, is verè pro Antichrifto fit cenfendus. Inveftigemus igitur eum hominem, qui geftat hanc notam Antichrifti, ut vel ex hac notâ, Antichriftum eum effe, deprehendamus. Quis eft igitur omnium hominum ufquam, qui & doctrinâ, & tota vitâ Chrifto adverfarius eft? Faciamus itaq; primùm inductionem aliquam partium doctrinæ Chrifti, ut ex oppofitâ doctrinâ Antichriftum deprehendamus. Primùm, doctrina Chrifti eft, ut Dominum noftrum Deum folum adoremus, eique foli ferviamus. Quis autem eft qui cultum Deo proprium communicat quoque Angelis, hominibus defunctis hac vita, imaginibus arte-factis, reliquiis mortuorum, inprimis autem panicio Deo in facrificio Miffæ? Annon is eft Pontifex Romanus? Secundò, Chriftus prohibet ἐθελοθρησκείας[?] & doctrinas inventas ac traditas ab hominibus in Dei cultu. Quis autem eft qui infinitas ἐθελοθρησκείας[?], traditiones & inventiones humanas, Ecclefiæ Chrifti obtrudit? Annon idem

page.notes: The Greek words σέβασμα and ἐθελοθρησκείας (both occurrences) are set in italic type and read from a small scan; their accents and letters are uncertain, so they are marked [?]. The small mark in the right margin beside "Quis" looks like a printer's pointing mark, not printed text, and is left out. The first line is cut at the left edge ("Opponct" may begin with a partly lost letter). The page ends mid-sentence with no catchword.
